CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER
The petitioners' land was acquired for the benefit of respondent No.1 under the provisions of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 (for short, "Act, 1966").
2. The petitioners were paid a sum of Rs.33,65,280/- as compensation for the acquisition of their land.
This amount was paid with the petitioners' consent under Section 29(2) of the Act, 1966.
Subsequently, the beneficiary agreed to pay an additional ex-gratia amount of Rs.2,61,54,720/-.

However, the release of the ex-gratia amount was delayed due to pending litigation concerning the subject land before this Court in W.P. No.8325/2012, which was disposed of on 18.06.2019 and later confirmed by a Division Bench of this Court in W.A. No.3656/2019 on 21.10.2022.
3.
The petitioners submitted an application dated 08.11.2022, requesting the release of the ex-gratia amount, which was eventually paid on 28.03.2023.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Union of India & Others v. C. Krishna Reddy [(2003) 12 SCC 627]
has held that no one has a legal right to claim a reward, as it is purely an ex-gratia payment subject to guidelines and at the absolute discretion of the competent authority.

entities.text: Union of India & Others v. C. Krishna Reddy [(2003) 12 SCC 627]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such payments cannot be claimed as a matter of right.

In the present case, compensation was paid based on the petitioners'
consent under Section 29(2) of the Act, 1966, and there was no contract between the petitioners and the beneficiary regarding the payment of interest on the ex-gratia amount.
Consequently, the petitioners' claim for interest on the ex- gratia amount is not sustainable.

sentences.text: The petitioners have also represented before the Special Land Acquisition Officer of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB), Mangaluru, requesting payment of the market value for the trees standing on the acquired land in Sy. No.188/A of Yellur village, Kaup Taluk.
6. The learned counsel for respondent-KIADB submitted that the entire compensation, including that related to standing trees, has already been settled.

7. In light of the above, the petition is disposed of with a direction to respondent No.2 to consider the representation dated 06.02.2024 submitted by the petitioners, as per Annexure-D annexed to I.A. No.3/2024.

Respondent No.2 NC: 2024:KHC:50482 shall pass an appropriate order in accordance with the law, after affording an opportunity of hearing to respondent No.1, within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
